meta.notes: attested=true means documented in colonial Spanish records as Taíno/Antillean, or a widely accepted Taíno→Spanish loan (hamaca, canoa, huracán, etc.). attested=false covers Neo-Taíno/community revival forms, comparative reconstructions, disputed Caribbean Spanish etymologies, and ethnohistoric names that are not Taíno lexemes. Classic Taíno is extinct (ISO tnq); revival mixes ages and invents forms—see ACCURACY.md. Learner SVO is pedagogical Neo-Taíno, not proven classical word order.
meta.disclaimer: This toolkit prefers colonial anchors and labels uncertainty. It is not a claim that reconstructed forms are Classical Taíno.

entries.definition_en: The Taíno name for Puerto Rico—literally 'native land' (bori + -ken).
entries.definition_es: El nombre taíno de Puerto Rico: literalmente 'tierra nativa' (bori + -ken).
entries.fun_fact: Saying Borikén is a tiny act of reclaiming the island's first name.

entries.definition_en: Originally meant 'good' or 'noble'; later used as the ethnonym for the people.
entries.definition_es: Originalmente significaba 'bueno' o 'noble'; luego se usó como nombre del pueblo.
entries.fun_fact: Columbus heard 'Taíno, Taíno' and thought it was their tribal name—it was a greeting of goodness.

entries.definition_en: A noun meaning 'village'. This form is attested in colonial records.

entries.definition_en: A community leader or chief responsible for guidance, diplomacy, and ceremony.
entries.definition_es: Líder o jefe comunitario responsable de guía, diplomacia y ceremonia.
entries.fun_fact: Spanish kept the word 'cacique' and still uses it today.

entries.definition_en: A round thatched house—the classic Taíno family dwelling.
entries.definition_es: Casa redonda de techo de paja—la vivienda familiar taína clásica.
entries.fun_fact: Walk into a bohío and you're inside island architecture 101.
entries.accuracy_note: Ethnohistoric / colonial lexical item widely cited for Taíno culture; orthography regularized.

entries.definition_en: A dugout boat carved from a single tree trunk, used for fishing and island travel.
entries.definition_es: Una embarcación tallada de un solo tronco, usada para pescar y viajar entre islas.
entries.fun_fact: 'Canoe' entered European languages from Taíno kanowa.

entries.definition_en: A hanging bed woven from plant fiber—perfect for island naps and trade voyages.
entries.definition_es: Una cama colgante tejida de fibra vegetal—ideal para siestas y viajes.
entries.fun_fact: Europeans had never seen hammocks before meeting Taíno communities.

entries.definition_en: A powerful storm; also linked to a fierce wind/storm spirit in Taíno cosmology.
entries.definition_es: Una tormenta poderosa; también ligada a un espíritu del viento en la cosmología taína.
entries.fun_fact: English 'hurricane' and Spanish 'huracán' both come from this word.

entries.definition_en: A raised wooden grill or frame for slow-cooking food over fire.
entries.definition_es: Una parrilla elevada de madera para cocinar lento sobre el fuego.
entries.fun_fact: Yes—barbecue is a Caribbean gift to the world.

entries.definition_es: Sustantivo que significa 'tabaco'. Forma atestiguada en crónicas coloniales. It entered Spanish (and often English) from Taíno.
entries.fun_fact: You already know a cousin of this word in Spanish: tabaco.

entries.spanish: Guarocuya (cacique; nombre de bautismo español Enriquillo)
entries.definition_en: Historical cacique of Hispaniola known in Spanish sources as Enriquillo (a baptismal name). His Indigenous name is often given as Guarocuya. This is ethnohistory, not a Taíno dictionary word.
entries.definition_es: Cacique histórico de La Española conocido en fuentes españolas como Enriquillo (nombre de bautismo). Su nombre indígena suele darse como Guarocuya. Es etnohistoria, no un lexema taíno de diccionario.
entries.fun_fact: Teaching tip: say Guarocuya for the person; never list Enriquillo as a Taíno stem.
entries.accuracy_note: Enriquillo / enrikíyo is a Spanish baptismal name, not a Taíno lexeme. Later tradition often gives the Indigenous name Guarocuya. Do not teach 'enrikíyo' as a Boriken vocabulary word.
entries.etymology: Spanish Enrique + diminutive; Indigenous name traditionally Guarocuya
